claims.sourceText: National Security Act of 1947, Public Law 80-253, 61 Stat. 495, sec. 102(d)(5), https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-61/pdf/STATUTE-61-Pg495.pdf
claims.text: Section 102(d)(5) of the same Act is the residual authority every later covert-action directive is written under: the Agency is 'to perform such other functions and duties related to intelligence affecting the national security as the National Security Council may from time to time direct.'

claims.sourceText: National Security Act of 1947, Public Law 80-253, ch. 343, 61 Stat. 495, secs. 101(a), 102(a), 201(a), approved 26 July 1947, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-61/pdf/STATUTE-61-Pg495.pdf
claims.text: The statute approved on 26 July 1947 creates, in one instrument, the Council, the Agency and the military establishment: 'There is hereby established a council to be known as the National Security Council'; 'There is hereby established under the National Security Council a Central Intelligence Agency with a Director of Central Intelligence, who shall be the head thereof'; 'There is hereby established the National Military Establishment, and the Secretary of Defense shall be the head thereof.'

claims.sourceText: National Security Act of 1947, Public Law 80-253, ch. 343, 61 Stat. 495, sec. 101(c), approved 26 July 1947, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-61/pdf/STATUTE-61-Pg495.pdf
claims.text: The second office is statutory. Section 101(c) of the National Security Act of 1947: 'The Council shall have a staff to be headed by a civilian executive secretary who shall be appointed by the President, and who shall receive compensation at the rate of $10,000 a year.'
